subject: Audit ledger + temporary retention exception — playbook and next steps
messages:
From: Sarah Wong <sarah.wong@atlashealth.com>
To: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@atlashealth.com
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask: audit ledger retention window + BYOK interaction

Hi Irene —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Two compliance items jumped out from our InfoSec review and I wanted to capture them here so we can sync:

1) Audit ledger retention: our auditors require an immutable audit ledger for admin actions and API access logs for 13 months. We understand Redwood has configurable audit exports but need details on timeline and guarantees (immutable / tamper-evident).
2) BYOK + ledger encryption: our policy is customer-managed keys for any audit artifacts stored outside our VPC. If the ledger export lands in Redwood-managed storage, we need a BYOK option or escrow pattern.

Can you confirm what’s feasible in the short term (pilot) vs. what’s product roadmap? Also attaching the compliance spec from our auditors.

Thanks —
Sarah Wong
Security PM, Atlas Health
Attachments: atlas-audit-specs.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Wong <sarah.wong@atlashealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask: audit ledger retention window + BYOK interaction

Sarah — thank you, this is helpful. I looped product and security ops so we can triage. Quick notes before we set a call: 

- We currently support configurable audit log retention and export. Exports can be pushed to a customer S3 (VPC endpoint) or to Redwood-managed blob storage. For an immutable ledger we rely on signed append-only exports plus integrity checks; we do not yet provide an HSM-backed ledger proof service.
- BYOK is available for model/key material in Private deployments; for hosted exports to Redwood-managed storage there is not an existing BYOK flow today.

Action items I’d like to cover in the triage:
- Define temporary exception pattern (13-month retention) and whether pushing exports into customer S3 satisfies auditors.
- Decide whether we can deliver a short-term BYOK export (customers supply envelope key for export at rest) vs. required roadmap work (HSM-backed ledger).
- Owner assignments for implementation and evidence pack.

Proposed times for a 30-min triage call: Mon 11/1 10am PT, Tue 11/2 11am PT. Which works for you?

— Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Product Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask: audit ledger retention window + BYOK interaction

Quick internal notes before the call — tagging technical constraints:

- Immutable ledger: current pipeline computes MD5/SHA256 for each export and stores checksums in our metadata DB. That gives tamper-evidence, but it's not equivalent to a signed append-only ledger (no global Merkle root).
- Export destinations: customer S3 (recommended for compliance) can be forced via route config; we can include object immutability (S3 Object Lock) if customer enables it.
- Short-term BYOK for exports: doable if Atlas provides a KMS key and we encrypt with a customer-provided envelope key client-side prior to upload. Requires a small client-side step or workload in Private. For hosted accounts we'd need to accept customer keys via a managed KMS integration (security review).

I'll bring a simple implementation sketch to the triage call — low effort: customer-managed S3 + Object Lock + checksum proofs. Medium effort: client-side envelope encryption flow. Long-term: HSM-backed ledger with signed roots.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Sarah Wong <sarah.wong@atlashealth.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2026 17:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial ask: audit ledger retention window + BYOK interaction

Thanks Sarah — we can do the 11/2 11am PT slot. Agenda proposal (20m triage + 10m next steps):

1) Confirm Atlas acceptance criteria (immutable vs tamper-evident) — Sarah to confirm.
2) Short-term pattern: customer S3 with Object Lock + checksum export. Responsibilities: Atlas enable S3 Object Lock and provide access role; Redwood provide export schedule and checksum manifest.
3) BYOK options: (a) client-side envelope encryption (pilot), (b) hosted KMS integration (security review, longer), (c) Private deployment (already supports customer KMS).
4) Evidence pack timeline & owner: list of artifacts Atlas needs for audit.

Deliverables: one-pager exception playbook and owner list + simple script for checksum verification.

Attachments: retention-exception-matrix.xlsx

— Marissa
Product Lead, Platform Integrations
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Wong <sarah.wong@atlashealth.com>

Cc: security@atlashealth.com
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2026 18:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial ask: audit ledger retention window + BYOK interaction

Thanks, team — 11/2 11am PT works. Quick clarifications ahead of the call:

- For our auditors immutable = copy cannot be altered and must be cryptographically verifiable. Object Lock + checksums is acceptable if we control the destination and Object Lock is enabled.
- For BYOK, Atlas prefers an approach where keys never transit Redwood-managed KMS; client-side envelope encryption before upload is acceptable. We can run a small job to push encrypted exports to Redwood S3 if needed.

Our asks on the call: sample manifest format, expected latency for export (daily vs near-real-time), and an initial evidence checklist.

— Sarah
Sarah Wong
Security PM, Atlas Health

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Wong <sarah.wong@atlashealth.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial ask: audit ledger retention window + BYOK interaction

Follow-up and short playbook draft (post-call notes):

Summary: Atlas will pilot the following pattern — customer-managed S3 bucket (VPC endpoint) with Object Lock + daily export from Redwood. Atlas will run a lightweight client-side encryptor that performs envelope encryption with their KMS key prior to upload. Redwood will produce a daily checksum manifest (SHA256 list) and a signed metadata file (signed with our service key) for each export batch.

Immediate deliverables (owners and ETA):
- Tech spec (export format, manifest schema) — owner: Ben Carter — ETA 11/12
- Example verification script + CI test — owner: Karthik Iyer — ETA 11/16
- Evidence checklist (signed metadata, export schedule, retention config) — owner: Marissa Cole — ETA 11/10
- Legal/contract exception language for hosted export to customer S3 — owner: Irene Choi (liaise with Sales) — ETA 11/13

Notes / risks:
- Signed metadata from Redwood provides provenance but is not a cryptographic Merkle root; if Atlas's auditors require an append-only root, that becomes a product roadmap ask.
- For hosted customers, accepting customer keys into our pipeline requires a security review; client-side encryptor avoids that, but adds operational burden to the customer.

Attachments referenced: audit-ledger-specs.pdf, retention-exception-matrix.xlsx

Next step: I'll drop the tech spec PR and the verification script prototype into the shared repo and ping the thread when ready.

— Karthik
Principal Engineer, Platform
Redwood Inference
